_comment: Per-game fixes for Settings > Games (helpers/game-fix). Each: the Steam app id, what it does, and files with the values to set. {width} and {height} are the screen's; paths: {game} {prefix} {userprofile} {localappdata} {documents}. Formats: kv (Key = value) and ini.

games.name: Dead Space 2
games.title: Full screen at your screen's size, ultrawide included
games.about: The game's own menu never lists 21:9 sizes and falls back to a 4:3 one (or 16:9 zoomed in). This writes your screen's size into its settings file (true 21:9, not stretched). Do not change the resolution in the game's menu afterwards: it would go back.
games.tip: Its own V-Sync locks it to 30 fps, and uncapped its physics break: with frame generation at 3x (180 Hz) the game runs at a steady 60 and the screen at 180.

games.name: Fallout 4
games.title: Your screen's size, borderless, and the settings files its launcher would make
games.about: Without its launcher's settings files the game starts at 1280x720. This makes them from the game's own templates and sets your screen's size, borderless full screen (the most reliable under Proton). At 21:9 the world is wider; the HUD and menus stay 16:9-shaped and stretched, which needs an interface mod.
games.tip: Its physics are tied to the frame rate and break above 60 fps: with frame generation at 3x (180 Hz) the game runs at 60 and the screen at 180.
